items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I recorded an album with the band of Raymond Fonseque... We recorded 10 original compositions of Fonsèque and myself

ctx.x: 1971 was going to be quite interesting, at least concerning traveling. I went back to Superbase,than to Switzerland, where I recorded two sides with the New Ragtime Band. Back in Paris, I recorded an album with the band of Raymond Fonseque,a very good trombonist who had a group of seven

musicians with piano, bass saxophone, banjo, washboard, clarinet and trumpet. Marcel Bornstein, who plays a very good trumpet, had played with Reveliott's band, and Sidney Bechet. We recorded 10 original compositions of Fonsèque and myself, and we were very pleased with the album which was different from other things that I have recorded. We nammed the album "Bill and the Boys" B.C. with Raymond Fonsèque and his Original Jazz Band.

In June, I participated in another French Festival located in Normandy, in a village called Luneray. This festival was taking place in a potato storage barn, and there was an attendance of 10,000 people in those days. Plenty of amateur bands were there, and 4 or 5 professional ones. Also, 2 or 3 wellknown artists as attraction. The music was non-stop from 10 in the morning until 9 in the evening. People could eat and drink there at a very moderate price.
